what_its_for: This medicine helps your immune system fight certain viral infections. It is most commonly used to treat chronic hepatitis B and chronic hepatitis C (often combined with another medicine called ribavirin). It works by boosting your body's natural defenses to slow down or stop the virus from multiplying.
how_to_take: Peginterferon alfa-2a comes as a liquid in a prefilled syringe or vial and is given as a shot just under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your stomach area, thigh, or upper arm. Your doctor or nurse will teach you how to give yourself the injection at home. Always rotate the injection site each week so you do not use the same spot twice in a row. Never shake the syringe. Use each prefilled syringe or vial only once and then throw it away safely in a puncture-resistant sharps container.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 180 micrograms (mcg) injected once a week, always on the same day each week. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects or kidney or blood cell problems. Treatment usually lasts 24 to 48 weeks depending on the type of hepatitis and how well the virus is responding. Always follow the exact dose and schedule your doctor prescribes — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and you remember within 2 days of when it was due, take the missed dose as soon as possible and then continue on your regular weekly schedule. If it has been more than 2 days since the missed dose, skip it and just take your next scheduled dose on the usual day. Do not take two doses in one week to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store peginterferon alfa-2a in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it — if it accidentally freezes, do not use it. Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not shake the syringe. Take it out of the refrigerator about 15 to 30 minutes before your injection to let it reach room temperature, which can make the injection more comfortable. Keep all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can worsen liver damage and reduce how well the treatment works. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness, confusion, or extreme tiredness. Avoid close contact with people who are sick, since this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections. Do not get live vaccines (such as live flu vaccine, MMR, or chickenpox vaccine) without first asking your doctor. If you are of childbearing age or your partner is, use effective birth control during treatment and for 6 months after, especially if you are also taking ribavirin, which can cause serious birth defects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of harming yourself or others, severe depression or mood changes, chest pain or irregular heartbeat, difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, signs of infection such as high fever or chills, vision changes or eye pain, severe stomach pain, signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) or dark urine, unusual bruising or bleeding, or a severe skin rash. Also call your doctor if you develop numbness or tingling, significant weight loss, or worsening fatigue that makes daily activities very difficult.
when_it_works: You may not feel any different right away — this medicine works slowly over several months. Blood tests will be done regularly to check if the virus levels are going down and to monitor your blood counts and liver function. Many people start to see improvement in virus levels after the first few weeks of treatment, but the full course of therapy (usually 24 to 48 weeks) is needed to get the best results. It is very important to finish the entire treatment even if you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution as side effects such as confusion or heart problems may be more likely. Kidney problems: Your dose may need to be reduced if your kidneys are not working well. Liver problems: This medicine is generally not recommended for people with severe or decompensated liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine should NOT be used during pregnancy. If you can become pregnant, you must use two reliable forms of birth control. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Children: Pegasys is not approved for use in children under 5 years old; dosing in children is based on body size and will be determined by your doctor. Depression or mental health history: Tell your doctor if you have ever had depression, anxiety, or other mental health conditions, as this medicine can make these worse.
